title: The Sharp knife on the board
subtitle: 仪表穿着 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）
meta: 主题语境：仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）　|　核心词汇：sharp　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sharp 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1984 the teacher wrote of ① a sharp knife on the board in the notebook, and everybody in the classroom said at once that it was ② sharper than the one named there the year before. Three terms on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the teacher, who never explained anything, had done it before dawn and gone home; it was the sharp ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the sharpest knife on the board anybody in the classroom had ever seen, or so the notebook for March 1978 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too sharp to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the pupil who had come to help; the sharp ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the ruler at the far blackboard, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a sharp eye of the tailor, and said that no pupil in his right mind would call it ⑥ as sharp as the eye of the tailor they had once had in the old classroom. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was sharp or not, and he said so.

By 1991 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the notebook. What the line asked for was ⑦ something sharp, and nothing besides. The pupil from the next classroom called the whole plan ⑧ quite sharp; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the notebook kept the names of the sharp ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1994, in public, she wrote of another sharp knife on the board in the same notebook, and the work, which took two terms, seemed ⑨ sharper than anybody had expected. ⑩ The sharpest eye of the tailor in the whole classroom, she said in 1996, was the one she could never quite name; the sharp ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 锋利（前置定语 a sharp knife on the board：1984 年先生在笔记簿里记下的那件锋利的刀）
B. adj. 锋利／敏锐（比较级 sharper than：文中两处，一处比案板上锋利的刀，一处比预想）
C. adj. 锋利／敏锐（最高级 the sharpest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 锋利（表语 too sharp to do：母亲觉得它太锋利，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 敏锐（前置定语 a sharp eye of the tailor：叔叔把整件事称作一桩敏锐的眼力）
F. adj. 敏锐（同级比较 as sharp as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩裁缝敏锐的眼力相比）
G. adj. 敏锐（后置定语 something sharp：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 敏锐（受程度副词修饰 quite sharp：那位学童的评价）

items.q: a sharp knife on the board
the sharpest knife on the board anybody
a sharp eye of the tailor
The sharpest eye of the tailor in

answers.why: sharp 意为“锋利”，1984 年先生在笔记簿里记下的是“一件锋利的刀”，此处作前置定语 a sharp knife on the board。
sharp 意为“锋利”，此处用比较级 sharper than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
sharp 意为“锋利”，笔记簿上 三月 那行字说它是教室里最锋利的一件，故用最高级 the sharpest knife on the board。
sharp 意为“锋利”，母亲认为这件东西“太锋利了，谁也用不上”，too sharp to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
sharp 意为“敏锐”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩敏锐的眼力”，此处作前置定语 a sharp eye of the tailor。
sharp 意为“敏锐”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩裁缝敏锐的眼力一样敏锐”，同级比较用 as sharp as。
sharp 意为“敏锐”，笔记簿上那半行字要的是“敏锐的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something sharp。
sharp 意为“敏锐”，邻教室来的那位学童认为这套计划“相当敏锐”，quite 修饰原级 sharp。
sharp 意为“敏锐”，1994 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要敏锐”，故用比较级 sharper than。
sharp 意为“敏锐”，母亲 1996 年说的是“整个教室里最敏锐的那一桩”，故用最高级 the sharpest eye of the tailor。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1984 年，先生在笔记簿里记下了一件锋利的刀。（a sharp knife on the board）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更锋利。（sharper than …）
母亲觉得它太锋利，谁也用不上。（too sharp to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩敏锐的眼力。（a sharp eye of the tailor）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩裁缝敏锐的眼力一样敏锐。（as sharp as …）
到了 1991 年，笔记簿上只剩半行字：要的是一件敏锐的东西。（something sharp）
answers: In 1984 the teacher wrote of a sharp knife on the board in the notebook.
Everybody said it was sharper than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too sharp to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a sharp eye of the tailor.
He said nobody would call it as sharp as the eye of the tailor they had once had.
By 1991 the notebook asked for nothing but something sharp.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 sharp 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1984 the teacher wrote of a sharp knife on the board in the notebook, and nobody forgot it.
It was the sharpest knife on the board in the classroom, or so the notebook says.
My mother thought it too sharp to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a sharp eye of the tailor, and nobody argued with him.
The pupil from the next classroom called the plan quite sharp, and everybody laughed.
The sharp ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
